items.name: Relative 2-rank bound for a quadratic extension
items.statement: For every quadratic extension E/F of number fields, let t count the ramified places of F, including real places that become complex, and put e=max(t,1). With r_2(L)=dim_F2(Cl(L)/2Cl(L)), one has r_2(E)≤2(r_2(F)+e−1), hence h_2(E)≤4^(e−1)h_2(F)^2.
items.locator: Klüners–Wang arXiv:2003.12161v2, Theorem 2.1 and proof, pp.3–4; Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C2
items.note: Apply quadratic-coinvariant-extension. If t>0, one order-two inertia lift splits G, so it is elementary abelian of rank s+1. Kill the at most t inertia generators; the quotient corresponds to an everywhere-unramified abelian extension of F and is a quotient of Cl(F), giving s+1−t≤r_2(F). If t=0, G itself is a quotient of Cl(F), and |2G|≤2 gives s≤dim(G/2G)≤r_2(F). Combine with r_2(E)≤2s. Preserve both branches and infinite inertia. This later auxiliary theorem replaces, but does not verify, the original one-factor relative-genus-source-claim. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: t=0 permits a C4 extension; t=1 gives r_2(E)≤2r_2(F); finite and real ramification are both counted.

items.name: Ramified places bounded by relative-discriminant support
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F with [F:Q]=m≥1 and relative discriminant ideal Δ_(E/F), the number t of finite and infinite ramified places of F satisfies t≤mω(N_F/Q Δ_(E/F))+m≤mω(D_E)+m. Here D_E=D_F² N_F/Q Δ_(E/F), and ω counts distinct rational prime divisors of a positive integer.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C3
items.note: Each finite ramified prime divides the relative discriminant, at most m primes of F lie above a rational prime, and at most m real places ramify. Import the actual ramification/discriminant-tower and prime-fiber bounds from their existing suppliers; exact generic declaration matching remains a blueprint obligation. Relative ideal discriminant, its positive rational norm, and the absolute field discriminant are separate quantities. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: relative discriminant norm one leaves only the infinite contribution; several prime ideals above one rational prime require the m factor; real-to-complex ramification is not silently dropped.

items.name: Uniform quadratic relative torsion bound with squared base factor
items.statement: For every m≥1 and η>0 there is C_(m,η)>0 such that every quadratic extension E/F with [F:Q]=m satisfies h_2(E)≤C_(m,η)D_E^η h_2(F)^2. The constant is uniform as the base field F varies. In particular h_2(Q)=1 gives h_2(E)≪_η D_E^η for quadratic fields E/Q.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C3–C4, deduced from Klüners–Wang Theorem 2.1
items.note: Exponentiate quadratic-relative-rank, use ramified-place-support, and absorb (4^m)^ω(D_E) with prime-support-loss; the infinite-place factor is degree-bounded. State h_2(Q)=1 separately through the existing class-group/PID supplier at blueprint time. This proof needs h_2(F)^2, not the unverified h_2(F) factor in the 2017 source. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: varying F at fixed m must not enter the implied constant; quadratic fields give the D^η base case; the ramification-free branch still retains the squared class-group factor.

items.name: The general-exponent torsion bound by induction on absolute degree
items.statement: For every n≥3 and ε>0 there is C_(n,ε)>0 such that every degree-n number field K has h_2(K)≤C_(n,ε)D_K^(1/2−1/(2n)+ε). This follows from two-torsion-no-index-two and quadratic-relative-torsion, with the quadratic D^η base case. A quartic field containing a quadratic subfield satisfies the stronger h_2(K)≪_ε D_K^ε.
items.locator: Fourth-checkpoint supplement in the companion report, C4; replacement completion of the general-exponent route in BSTTTZ §4
items.note: Strong induction on n, not an assumption that every field has a quadratic tower to Q. With α_d=1/2−1/(2d), an index-two subfield F of degree m=n/2≥2 gives h_2(K)≪D_K^η D_F^(2α_m+2η)≤D_K^(α_m+2η), since D_F²≤D_K. The gain α_n−α_m=1/(2n)>0 and η=ε/4 suffice. For m=1 use the quadratic base case; for quartics with a quadratic subfield apply that base estimate with a suitably smaller η to both factors. This does not establish the sharper cubic exponent or the remaining quartic resolvent branch. Owner: EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion. Tests: degree three has no index-two branch; degree four uses m=2; no quadratic subfield means the norm-curve branch, not a nonexistent induction step.

items.name: Integer-preserving normalization of a bounded-slope graph
items.statement: Let N≥1 and let g be C-infinity near a compact interval I of length at most N, with |g′|≤1. If its graph has at least two integral points, restrict I to the interval between their least and greatest integer abscissae. Integer translations of the two coordinates then put the new interval inside [0,N] and the graph inside [0,N]×[−N,N], preserving every counted integral point, total degree and absolute irreducibility of a defining polynomial.
items.locator: BP1 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; expands Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 proof, author preprint pp.15–16.
items.note: Choose the vertical integer nearest the midpoint of the range; the new absolute value is ≤N/2+1/2≤N. Zero/one-point cases are separate. No arbitrary real translation of the lattice is allowed. For 0<N<1 use at most one integer abscissa instead. This is a lemma about the existing real interval and polynomial carriers, not a new definition. Tests: noninteger original interval endpoints; graph y=x+M for large integer M; N=1 and the zero/one-point branches. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods.

items.name: Stopping a determinant recurrence below lattice scale
items.statement: Let G:(0,∞)→[0,∞), α>0, H≥0, K≥1 and 0<λ<1 with Kλ^α=1/2. Suppose G(x)≤Hx^α+KG(λx) for x≥1 and G(x)≤1 for 0<x<1. Then G(N)≤(2H+K)N^α≤2(H+K)N^α for every N≥1.
items.locator: BP3 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 recurrence, author preprint pp.16–17.
items.note: For the least m with λ^mN<1, iterate m times. The residual term K^m equals 2^(−m)λ^(−mα) and is ≤2^(1−m)KN^α≤KN^α because λ^mN≥λ. The geometric sum is ≤2. Tests: N=1; λ^(m−1)N=1 with strict termination only at the next step; H=0. This numerical recurrence uses existing real powers and finite sums; no new generic owner.

items.name: Uniform determinant recurrence constants
items.statement: Let integers d≥2 and δ≥2d satisfy D=d(δ−d+1), p=d(δ(δ+1)−d(d−1))/2 and 0≤q≤p. Put α=2p/(D(D−1)), K=2d^4δ², λ=(2K)^(−1/α), A=(2/λ)^(D−1), X=(D^p A^q)^(2/(D(D−1))) and H=4d^5δ³X. Then Kλ^α=1/2 and H+K≤δ^(9dδ)/2. Consequently a graph-count function satisfying the preceding recurrence obeys G(N)≤N^(1/d)exp(4 log(N)/δ+9dδ log δ) for N≥1.
items.locator: BP4 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4 proof, author preprint pp.16–17.
items.note: Use 1/d≤α≤1/d+4/δ≤2, D≤dδ and X≤(DA)^α. The full inequality chain is in BP4, not a numerical approximation. Choose the worst case q=p when taking a maximum over polynomials, so H is uniform in their leading monomials. Derivative partitions give at most K intervals; the small-norm contribution is ≤HN^α and the remaining pieces have length ≤λN. Source issue E2 corrects the printed p≤q. Tests: d=2, δ=4; every possible leading Y-degree; the q=0 and q=p endpoints.

items.name: Integer parameter giving the Bombieri–Pila constant eleven
items.statement: For an integer d≥2 and N≥exp(d^6), put L=log N, ell=log L, S=sqrt(d L ell), x=2 sqrt(L/(d ell)) and δ=floor x. Then δ≥2d and 4L/δ+9dδ log δ≤11S.
items.locator: BP5 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; repairs the unstated integer rounding in Bombieri–Pila Theorem 4, author preprint p.17.
items.note: The proof is analytic, not inferred from testing: δ≥3x/4 and δ≥L^(1/4); E(t)=4L/t+9dt log t has E′(t)≥(17/36)d ell+9d>0 on [δ,x]. Thus E(δ)≤E(x)=S[11+(9/ell)log(4/(d ell))]≤11S. BP5 proves all threshold inequalities, using log d≤d/2. Source issue E3 records the gap, not a false theorem. Tests: d=2 and log N=64; both sides of integer jumps of x; large d at the threshold.

items.name: A singularity-safe cover for the integral-point theorem
items.statement: For N>0 and an absolutely irreducible real plane polynomial F of total degree d≥2, its integral zeros in [0,N]² are covered by at most 8d³ sets, each either a singleton or contained in a C-infinity graph on a compact subinterval of [0,N] with absolute slope at most one relative to one coordinate axis. Each graph satisfies F, or F with coordinates exchanged. For N≥exp(d^6), the constant-eleven graph bound therefore implies the constant-twelve plane-curve bound.
items.locator: BP6 of the sixth-checkpoint supplement; replacement for the abbreviated final passage of Bombieri–Pila Theorem 5, author preprint p.17.
items.note: Use proper Bézout on F_Y, F_X+F_Y and F_X−F_Y, and horizontal boundary intersections. There are at most Q=3d(d−1)+2d critical abscissae. Each open strip has at most d simple analytic root graphs; invert steep ones, and restrict each to the compact hull of its finitely many integer points. Critical vertical fibers contribute at most d points each. The total is ≤d(Q+1)+d(Q+2)≤8d³; log(8d³)≤sqrt(d log N loglog N) absorbs it. No smoothness at the original singular endpoints is assumed. Generic proper-intersection/Bézout stays with SF.5; exact root-continuation and analytic inverse-function supplier matching remains G7. This does not prove the stronger O(d²) whole-curve claim. Tests: singular cusp Y²=X³; steep graphs needing axis exchange; integral points on critical/boundary vertical fibers. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods. S1–S3 now prove nonzero coordinate specialization and the ≤d fiber count. Proper Bézout and smooth root continuation remain open.

items.name: Taylor remainder on a nondegenerate real interval
items.statement: For f:ℝ→ℝ, n∈ℕ and a≠b, ContDiffOn ℝ (n+1) f (uIcc a b) implies that some c∈uIoo a b satisfies f(b)−taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc a b) a b = iteratedDeriv (n+1) f c · (b−a)^(n+1)/(n+1)!.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/Taylor.lean:348–363
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Set n=k−1 in bp-large-derivative-interval; a=b is a separate trivial case. This exactly supplies the generic remainder, not BP's scaled inequality. Tests: k=1; a=b bypass; f(x)=x^k. No Lean instantiation run. Eighth checkpoint (Claude Code, cc-7b31c4): the two adapters this note previously left open are now closed against the same pin, and the closure is written out in the report section “Eighth checkpoint: the Taylor endpoint adapter”. (i) The endpoint conversion needs no neighbourhood of the endpoint: Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:70, iteratedDerivWithin_eq_iteratedDeriv (hs : UniqueDiffOn 𝕜 s) (h : ContDiffAt 𝕜 n f x) (hx : x ∈ s), has no interiority hypothesis, so with Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/TangentCone/Real.lean:102, uniqueDiffOn_uIcc (hab : a ≠ b), it applies at the endpoint a ∈ uIcc a b whenever f is ContDiffAt there. With taylorCoeffWithin (Taylor.lean:62), taylorWithinEval_succ (Taylor.lean:87) and taylor_within_zero_eval (Taylor.lean:100) this rewrites taylorWithinEval f n (uIcc a b) a b as the ordinary Taylor sum ∑_{j≤n} (j!)^{-1} · iteratedDeriv j f a · (b−a)^j. (ii) The a=b case is taylorWithinEval_self (Taylor.lean:109), which gives both sides f a with zero remainder, so the a ≠ b hypothesis of the two cited Taylor lemmas is not a gap. What remains for BP2's scaled inequality is only the supremum step: ContDiffOn.continuousOn_iteratedDerivWithin (IteratedDeriv/Defs.lean:147) on an open U ⊇ uIcc a b, with IsOpen.uniqueDiffOn (TangentCone/Basic.lean:291) and the same conversion, makes iteratedDeriv (n+1) f continuous on uIcc a b, and IsCompact.exists_isMaxOn (Topology/Order/Compact.lean:246) with isCompact_Icc supplies the maximum. No Lean instantiation is claimed for any of this; the hypothesis actually used is C^{n+1} smoothness on an open set containing uIcc a b, which is stronger than the ContDiffOn hypothesis of the cited remainder lemma and is what BP2's polynomial and algebraic-branch setting provides. Tenth checkpoint: the endpoint conversion is now a separately linked missing application bp-taylor-endpoint; the maximum-of-absolute-derivative bound is bp-taylor-absolute-bound. BP2 itself uses the kth-derivative lower bound at its Taylor witness, not the supremum upper bound. The earlier sentence calling only a supremum step the remaining BP2 proof is superseded by this distinction.

items.name: Existence and uniqueness of polynomial interpolation
items.statement: For a field F, finite index set s, nodes v injective on s and values r, Lagrange.interpolate s v r evaluates to r(i) at v(i), has polynomial degree strictly less than #s, and is the unique polynomial with those properties.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Lagrange.lean:295–379
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Generic interpolation for the derivative-determinant proof, not the derivative-witness or factorial estimate. The empty set uses degree(0)=bottom, not a false natural-degree <0 assertion. Distinct-node hypotheses must be retained; repeated graph abscissae are removed before interpolation. Tests: empty set gives zero; one node gives its constant value; duplicate nodes cannot invoke the uniqueness theorem. Reuse Lagrange.interpolate, do not define another carrier.

items.name: Vandermonde determinant and distinct-node criterion
items.statement: For a commutative ring R and v:Fin n→R, det(Matrix.vandermonde v)=∏i∏j>i(v(j)−v(i)). If R is an integral domain, this determinant is nonzero exactly when v is injective.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Vandermonde.lean:219–235
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. The matrix has entries v(i)^j. This supplies the algebraic factor of bp-derivative-determinant; it does not supply divided differences, derivative witnesses or the analytic bound. Tests: n=0 has empty determinant/product one; two nodes give v(1)−v(0); repeated nodes give zero.

items.name: Too many distinct roots force a polynomial to vanish
items.statement: For a polynomial p over a commutative integral domain, a finite type ι and an injective f:ι→R, if p.eval(f(i))=0 for every i and p.natDegree<Fintype.card ι, then p=0. Consequently a nonzero univariate polynomial cannot vanish on a finite set of more than its natural degree distinct elements.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/Roots.lean:740–755
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Apply contrapositively to the specialized polynomial F(a,Y) in bp-explicit-graph-cover. The adapter must prove this specialization is nonzero and its degree ≤d. Absolute irreducibility and total degree d≥2 exclude the vertical linear component; root counting alone does not. Also supplies the polynomial-branch case in bp-derivative-partition. Tests: nonzero constant has no zeros; p=X^d has one distinct zero; p=0 must be excluded from the counting corollary.

items.name: Derivative bound gives a Lipschitz estimate on a convex set
items.statement: For 𝕜 real or complex, a normed 𝕜-vector space G, convex s⊂𝕜, f differentiable at every point of s, and ‖deriv f x‖≤C on s, any x,y∈s satisfy ‖f y−f x‖≤C‖y−x‖.
items.locator: Generic input to Bombieri–Pila selected proof path pp.1–6,14–17; Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/MeanValue.lean:728–733
items.note: Codex codex-a71f92 read the actual declaration statement at Mathlib pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. Specialize to ℝ→ℝ, C=1 and a closed interval for bp-integer-normalization. Its smooth-neighbourhood assumption gives differentiability at the endpoints, avoiding an unjustified within/ordinary-derivative conversion. The estimate bounds the range diameter; compactness and nearest-integer translation are further inputs, not conclusions of this theorem. Tests: constant graph; slope-one graph; singleton interval.

items.name: Rank-nullity for finite-dimensional source
items.statement: For a division ring K, K-vector spaces V,W with V finite-dimensional and a linear map T:V→ₗ[K]W, finrank K (range T)+finrank K (ker T)=finrank K V. No finite-dimensionality of W is required.
items.note: Actual statement read at pin 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174. The rank of the rectangular evaluation matrix is matched separately via Matrix.rank; polynomial nonzeroness is not a conclusion of rank-nullity alone.

items.name: Rolle's theorem with an actual derivative
items.statement: For real a<b and f,f':ℝ→ℝ, if f is continuous on [a,b], f(a)=f(b), and HasDerivAt f (f'(x)) x for every x∈(a,b), then some c∈(a,b) has f'(c)=0.
items.note: Statement read at the pin. Use the HasDerivAt form so that a totalized zero derivative at a nondifferentiable point cannot masquerade as an analytic witness. The repeated application is bp-iterated-rolle, still missing.

items.name: Attainment of a continuous real maximum
items.statement: For a nonempty compact set S in a topological space and a continuous real-valued function h on S, there is x∈S with h(y)≤h(x) for all y∈S.
items.locator: Mathlib/Topology/Order/Compact.lean:246–249; generic input to Bombieri–Pila scaled derivative norms p.3.
items.note: Exact real-codomain specialization of the declaration read at the pin. Apply to h=|f^(r)|, not h=f^(r) followed by absolute value. Compactness of a closed real interval is isCompact_Icc; continuity and nonemptiness remain explicit hypotheses.

items.name: Coefficient coordinates for restricted polynomial support
items.statement: For a field F and finite set M of exponents in Fin 2→₀ℕ, Φ_M:F^M→{Q∈MvPolynomial (Fin 2) F | support Q⊆M}, c↦Σ_(m∈M)monomial m(c_m), is a linear equivalence with inverse Q↦(coeff_m Q)_(m∈M). At every indexed point z_s, evaluation of Φ_M(c) equals (A.mulVec c)_s for A_(s,m)=z_s^m.
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila Lemmas 1,3, pp.2–3,11; checkpoint ten R1.
proofSteps: The coefficient-sum and coefficient-monomial identities give coeff_e Φ_M(c)=c_e on M and 0 off M.
The existing monomial basis reconstructs any polynomial from its finitely supported coefficient vector; if its support is contained in M the reconstruction sum may be indexed by M.
Linearity and the inverse identities follow coefficientwise. Apply eval₂_sum and eval₂_monomial with identity coefficient homomorphism to obtain the matrix-vector evaluation identity.
acceptance: M empty gives the zero vector space and zero polynomial.
A nonzero coefficient vector produces a nonzero polynomial regardless of the chosen points.
Duplicate point indices are allowed; duplicate exponent indices are not.
items.note: Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods. This promotes the consumed coefficient/evaluation API, not a new polynomial carrier.

items.name: An iterated Rolle witness from ordered zeros
items.statement: For n≥1, real nodes a_0<...<a_n, an open U containing [a_0,a_n], and h:ℝ→ℝ of class C^n on U with h(a_i)=0 for all i, there is ξ∈(a_0,a_n) with iteratedDeriv n h ξ=0.
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila p.5 mean-value passage; checkpoint ten R2.
proofSteps: For each r<n, the rth derivative is continuous and differentiable on U: use the within-derivative statements on the open set and convert with iteratedDerivWithin_of_isOpen.
Starting with the n+1 ordered zeros, apply the HasDerivAt Rolle supplier between adjacent zeros to produce n strictly interleaving zeros of h'.
Repeat on adjacent zeros of the next derivative. After n rounds there is one zero of h^(n), strictly between the original extreme nodes. Every new closed subinterval remains in U.
acceptance: n=1 is precisely Rolle's theorem.
For n=0 one only has h(a_0)=0, not a witness in an empty open interval; consumers handle it separately.
Strict interleaving preserves distinctness for the next induction round.
items.note: Application adapter owned by IntegralPointDeterminantMethods; reuse generic calculus. No new general calculus roadmap or library status is asserted.

items.name: Leading interpolation coefficient as a normalized derivative
items.statement: For n≥1, real a_0<...<a_n, open U⊇[a_0,a_n], f of class C^n on U, and p=Lagrange.interpolate at these n+1 nodes with values f(a_i), some ξ∈(a_0,a_n) satisfies coeff_n p=f^(n)(ξ)/n!. Thus if |f^(n)(x)|/n!≤B throughout the interval, |coeff_n p|≤B. For n=0 the interpolant is the constant f(a_0).
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila p.5, following Proposition 2; checkpoint ten R3.
proofSteps: Interpolation gives degree p≤n and f−p vanishing at all n+1 nodes. Polynomial evaluation is smooth, so apply bp-iterated-rolle to f−p.
Polynomial.deriv and iteratedDeriv_succ identify analytic iterated derivatives with evaluations of iterated formal derivatives.
The formal coefficient formula shows derivative^[n] p is the constant n! coeff_n p: its constant coefficient is n! coeff_n p, and every positive coefficient vanishes since degree p≤n.
The derivative of f−p at the Rolle point is zero; divide by the nonzero real factorial. The n=0 case follows from the singleton interpolation formula.
acceptance: The polynomial X³ on four nodes has coefficient 1 and third derivative 6.
For x² and x³ on nodes 0,1, the first-derivative witnesses are respectively 1/2 and 1/√3, hence cannot be shared.
A singleton interpolation does not require an interior witness.
items.note: Witnesses are entrywise: each prefix of nodes and each column function can have a different ξ. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods.

items.name: Newton interpolation factorization of an evaluation determinant
items.statement: Over a field F, let D≥1 and x_0,...,x_(D−1) be pairwise distinct. For arbitrary values Y_(i,j), let p_(r,j) interpolate the first r+1 values in column j and B_(r,j)=coeff_r p_(r,j). Put W_r(X)=∏_(t<r)(X−x_t) and L_(i,r)=W_r(x_i). Then Y=L B and det Y=(∏_(t<i)(x_i−x_t)) det B.
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila Proposition 2 pp.4–5, expressed with existing Lagrange interpolation; checkpoint ten R4.
proofSteps: For r=0, p_(0,j) is constant B_(0,j). For r≥1, subtract p_(r−1,j)+B_(r,j)W_r from p_(r,j). The degree-r term cancels, and the resulting polynomial of degree<r vanishes at the first r distinct nodes; interpolation uniqueness makes it zero.
Induction gives p_(D−1,j)=Σ_(r<D)B_(r,j)W_r. Evaluating at all nodes proves Y=L B.
For i<r, W_r(x_i)=0; the diagonal is ∏_(t<i)(x_i−x_t). Use the existing lower-triangular determinant and determinant multiplication identities.
acceptance: D=1 has L=(1) and Vandermonde factor 1.
The formula holds for arbitrary value matrices, including singular matrices.
Transposing the evaluation convention requires transposing both factors; no silent orientation change is allowed.
items.note: No new Newton polynomial carrier is introduced: W_r is an explicit product in F[X]. The adapter is missing even though its interpolation and determinant ingredients are library declarations.

items.name: Ordinary Taylor expansion from neighbourhood smoothness
items.statement: For n∈ℕ, a≠b, an open U containing uIcc(a,b), and f:ℝ→ℝ of class C^(n+1) on U, there is ξ∈uIoo(a,b) with f(b)−Σ_(j=0)^n f^(j)(a)(b−a)^j/j!=f^(n+1)(ξ)(b−a)^(n+1)/(n+1)!. If a=b the ordinary sum is f(a) and the remainder is zero, with no interior witness asserted.
items.locator: Eighth-checkpoint T1–T2, integrated and rechecked in checkpoint ten R5; Bombieri–Pila Lemma 7 p.14.
proofSteps: For a≠b, uIcc(a,b) has UniqueDiffOn. Openness gives ContDiffAt at the endpoint a through each required order.
Apply iteratedDerivWithin_eq_iteratedDeriv at a∈uIcc(a,b); the interval need not be a neighbourhood of a.
Use taylorCoeffWithin, the successor evaluation formula and the zero-order evaluation formula to expand the within-Taylor polynomial as the ordinary derivative sum.
Restrict smoothness to uIcc(a,b) and apply bp-taylor-supplier. For a=b the self-evaluation identity and powers of zero give a zero remainder separately.
acceptance: n=0 is the ordinary first-derivative mean-value remainder.
A singleton interval cannot satisfy UniqueDiffOn_uIcc via a≠b; it is a separate branch.
No conversion from mere closed-interval ContDiffOn to ordinary endpoint derivatives is asserted.
items.note: Credits the eighth checkpoint's existing proof rather than claiming its invention. Owner: IntegralPointDeterminantMethods; no Lean elaboration.

items.name: Taylor remainder bounded by the absolute derivative maximum
items.statement: Under bp-taylor-endpoint's neighbourhood smoothness hypotheses, allowing a=b, there is an attained M=max_(x∈uIcc(a,b))|f^(n+1)(x)|≥0 and |f(b)−Σ_(j=0)^n f^(j)(a)(b−a)^j/j!|≤M |b−a|^(n+1)/(n+1)!.
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila scaled norms p.3 and derivative estimate p.5; checkpoint ten R6.
proofSteps: On open U, continuousOn_iteratedDerivWithin and iteratedDerivWithin_of_isOpen give continuity of the ordinary (n+1)st derivative; compose with absolute value and restrict to the closed interval.
The interval is compact and nonempty even when a=b. Apply bp-absolute-maximum-supplier to the absolute-value function; let M be its attained value.
For unequal endpoints, take absolute values of bp-taylor-endpoint and bound the value at ξ by M. For equal endpoints the remainder and length factor are zero.
acceptance: For f=−x³ on [1,2], n=1, the remainder has magnitude 4, M=12, and the bound is 6. Replacing M by |max f''|=6 would give the false bound 3.
For f a polynomial of degree≤n the remainder is zero.
Equal endpoints require neither a Rolle point nor unique derivatives within the singleton.
items.note: This upper remainder bound is distinct from the lower derivative estimate used by bp-large-derivative-interval. The compact-maximum argument also supplies attainment for each derivative order of bp-scaled-derivative-norm.

items.name: An injective vector-space map has a linear retraction
items.statement: For vector spaces over a division ring, ker(f)=⊥ implies existence of a linear g with g.comp f=id. With finite coordinate bases, toMatrix converts composition to matrix multiplication.

items.name: Expand a determinant over finite row combinations
items.statement: The determinant is alternating multilinear in its rows. Multilinear maps expand a tuple of finite sums over all choices of one summand per coordinate and pull out the product of scalars. Repeated rows give determinant zero; the empty determinant is one.

items.name: Leibniz formula for iterated ordinary derivatives
items.statement: For C^n functions f,g at x into a normed algebra, iteratedDeriv n(fg)(x)=Σ_(i=0)^n choose(n,i) iteratedDeriv i f(x) iteratedDeriv(n−i)g(x). The identity-function derivative is x in order zero, one in order one, and zero in higher orders.

items.name: Binomial coefficients cancel normalized derivative factorials
items.statement: For k≤n, choose(n,k) k! (n−k)!=n!. Casting into R and dividing by the nonzero factorials yields the normalized Leibniz convolution.

items.name: Factor theorem over an arbitrary commutative coefficient ring
items.statement: For a polynomial p over a commutative ring and an element a of that ring, X−C(a) divides p iff p(a)=0. Apply with coefficient ring K[Y] and a the constant polynomial.

items.name: Units of a multivariate polynomial ring over a reduced ring
items.statement: Over a reduced commutative ring R, P is a unit iff P=C(r) for a unit r of R. In particular over a field every polynomial unit is a nonzero constant.

items.name: Existing polynomial coordinate equivalences
items.statement: finSuccEquiv R n identifies MvPolynomial (Fin(n+1)) R with Polynomial(MvPolynomial (Fin n) R), taking variable zero to the outer variable and successor variables to constant coefficients. uniqueAlgEquiv identifies one-variable MvPolynomial with Polynomial R.

api.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.outer
api.statement: Use finSuccEquiv K 1 to regard X as the outer polynomial variable and Y as the coefficient-ring variable.

api.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.one
api.statement: Use uniqueAlgEquiv K (Fin 1) for the residual one-variable polynomial; its inverse and coefficient identities are the existing equivalence API.

api.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.specialize
api.statement: Evaluate the outer variable at the constant a, then apply the one-variable equivalence; polynomial operations and constant coefficients are preserved.

tests.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.x
tests.statement: finSuccEquiv K 1 (X 0)=Polynomial.X.

tests.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.y
tests.statement: finSuccEquiv K 1 (X 1)=Polynomial.C (MvPolynomial.X 0).

tests.name: IntegralPointBounds.polynomialCoordinates.monomial
tests.statement: uniqueAlgEquiv maps the one-variable monomial with exponent j and coefficient c to Polynomial.monomial j c.

uses.how: Apply the actual ring factor theorem in the outer variable and transport divisibility back.

items.name: A full-column-rank evaluation matrix has a nonzero row minor
items.statement: For a field K, finite column type M of cardinality D and finite row type S, if A:S×M→K has rank D, then there is an injection ρ:M→S with det(A.submatrix ρ id)≠0. Includes D=0 with the empty determinant one.
proofSteps: Rank-nullity gives ker(A.mulVecLin)=0. The linear retraction supplier gives B with BA=I_D; use coordinate-matrix composition, not a square-only inverse theorem.

Write each row of BA as Σ_s B_(i,s) A_(s,−). Multilinearity gives 1=Σ_(ρ:M→S)(∏_i B_(i,ρ(i))) det(A_(ρ(i),j)). This follows directly from map_sum and map_smul_univ; no unverified rectangular Cauchy–Binet declaration is assumed.

Since the finite sum is nonzero, some summand is nonzero, hence so is its determinant. A repeated row would make that determinant zero, so ρ is injective. For M empty the unique map is injective and the determinant is one.
acceptance: A 3-by-2 matrix with rows (1,0),(0,0),(0,1) needs rows 1 and 3, not the first two rows.
If S is empty and D>0 full column rank cannot hold.
Duplicate indexed points are permitted; they simply cannot both occur in the selected nonzero minor.

items.name: Normalized derivatives give the scaled product estimate
items.statement: For N>0, nonempty compact I⊂[0,N], an open neighbourhood U, k≥0 and m≥1 real functions f_1,...,f_m of class C^k on U, ||∏f_j||_(N,k;I)≤N^(m−1)(k+1)^(m−1)∏||f_j||_(N,k;I).
proofSteps: Divide the binary Leibniz formula by r!: (fg)^(r)/r!=Σ_(i=0)^r (f^(i)/i!)(g^(r−i)/(r−i)!). Factorial cancellation uses the exact natural identity cast to R.
For each summand the two norm bounds give |f^(i)g^(r−i)|/(i!(r−i)!)≤B_f B_g N^(2−r). Multiply by N^(r−1) and sum r+1 nonnegative bounds, giving ≤N(k+1)B_fB_g for r≤k.
Take the maximum over r,x. Induct on m starting with m=1; products remain C^k on the same open neighbourhood. This never assumes that a zero norm is invertible.
acceptance: For k=0 and constants c_j the factor N^(m−1) is necessary and the bound is equality.
Zero factors and singleton I cause no division problem.
The empty product m=0 is not included and is treated separately as the constant function one.

items.name: Monomial derivative bounds with the constant treated separately
items.statement: For the same data and H=||f||_(N,k;I), if i+j≥1 then ||x^i f^j||≤((k+1)N)^(i+j−1)H^j. For i=j=0 the exact norm is 1/N.
items.locator: Bombieri–Pila Proposition 1 and Lemmas 2/4; continuation D2
proofSteps: The norm of id on I⊂[0,N] is at most one, by the exact iterated derivatives. It equals one if k≥1; for k=0 a strict subinterval can have norm less than one.
Apply the m=i+j product estimate to i copies of id and j copies of f, allowing i=0 or j=0 as long as m≥1.
The constant monomial is the empty product and has norm 1/N. Do not substitute i+j=0 into the positive-factor product estimate.
acceptance: For k=1 the unsupported empty-product substitution would give 1/(2N), contradicting ||1||=1/N.
The pure monomials x^i and f^j are covered without assuming both exponents positive.
For H=0 and j>0 the monomial vanishes on I.

items.name: The monomial determinant bound retains D^p including the constant column
items.statement: Let M be D≥2 distinct bivariate monomials, p=Σ(i+j), q=Σj, H=||f||_(N,D−1;I), and x_1,...,x_D distinct in an interval of length L inside I. Then |det(x_r^i f(x_r)^j)|≤L^(D(D−1)/2) D^p H^q N^(p−D(D−1)/2). If the determinant is a nonzero integer, its norm is ≥1, so D^p H^q>0 and the separation bound of bp-integral-determinant follows.
proofSteps: Let z be one if (0,0)∈M and zero otherwise. The product of the monomial norms is ≤N^(p−D) D^(p−D+z) H^q. Exponents may be negative integers, and N,D are positive.
The determinant bound contributes D! N^(D(3−D)/2). Since D!=1·2···D≤D^(D−1) and z≤1, D! D^(p−D+z)≤D^p. Thus the missing factor for the constant monomial is absorbed without changing the stated D^p.

The Vandermonde factor is ≤L^(D(D−1)/2). Combine N exponents to p−D(D−1)/2. For a nonzero integer determinant, 1≤|det| forces H^q>0, so the positive-real power rearrangement is valid. If H=0,q>0 every column with positive Y exponent is zero; no full-rank block exists.
acceptance: M={1,x} has the constant monomial and determinant x_2−x_1; no loss of a factor D is allowed.
M={x,x²} has no constant monomial and satisfies the same bound.
The convention H^0=1 permits q=0 even when H=0; repeated abscissae give zero determinant separately.

items.name: An irreducible nonlinear plane polynomial has no identically zero coordinate fiber
items.statement: For any field K, irreducible F∈K[X,Y] of total degree d≥2 and a∈K, both F(a,Y) and F(X,a) are nonzero polynomials. Absolute irreducibility is not needed for this algebraic step.
items.locator: Adapter for the BP6 finite graph cover; continuation S1
proofSteps: Regard F as a polynomial in X over K[Y] using the existing coordinate equivalences. If F(a,Y)=0, the factor theorem gives F=(X−a)G in K[X,Y].
X−a is a nonunit: evaluation at X=a would send a hypothetical inverse identity to 0=1. Irreducibility of F therefore forces G to be a unit.
The multivariate unit supplier makes G a nonzero constant. Thus F is a nonzero scalar multiple of X−a and has total degree at most one, contradicting d≥2. Exchange X,Y for the horizontal statement.
acceptance: F=X−a is a degree-one counterexample and is excluded.
F=(X−a)Y is a reducible degree-two counterexample, so the degree hypothesis alone is insufficient.
F=Y²−X has nonzero specialization Y²−a for every a, including a=0 with a repeated root.

items.name: Coordinate specialization does not increase total degree
items.statement: For any bivariate polynomial F over a field K and a∈K, natDegree(F(a,Y))≤totalDegree F, and similarly for F(X,a); the statement permits the zero specialization.
items.locator: Coefficient adapter for the finite-fiber bound; continuation S2
proofSteps: Write F as the finite sum Σ c_(i,j) X^iY^j using its actual support. Each supported pair satisfies i+j≤totalDegree F by le_totalDegree.
The coefficient of Y^j after X=a is Σ_i c_(i,j)a^i. If j>totalDegree F every summand is zero, so that coefficient vanishes. Cancellation can lower degree but cannot introduce a higher exponent.
A polynomial whose coefficients above d vanish has natural degree at most d; zero has natural degree zero and d≥0. Apply the same coefficient argument after exchanging the variables.
acceptance: Specialization can lower degree: XY+1 at X=0 gives 1.
Specialization can vanish: (X−a)Y at X=a; nonzeroness must come from S1 before root counting.
For Y^d+X at X=0 the bound is attained.

items.name: At most d points on each vertical or horizontal fiber
items.statement: For an irreducible F∈K[X,Y] of total degree d≥2 over a field K, each finite set of distinct zeros on a fixed vertical or horizontal line has cardinality ≤d. In particular this bounds the real and integral fibers used in BP6.
proofSteps: Fix X=a. S1 gives a nonzero univariate polynomial and S2 bounds its natural degree by d.
If a finite distinct set of roots had cardinality >d, the pinned root-count supplier would force that polynomial to vanish, contradicting S1.
Swap the coordinates for the horizontal version. This does not give a smooth branch parametrization or a two-curve Bézout theorem.
acceptance: A singular fiber with a repeated root is still bounded by the number of distinct roots.
No smoothness or characteristic-zero hypothesis is used in this fiber count.
Irreducible univariate F(X) of degree≥2 can have no K-rational vertical zero fiber; the same argument covers this degenerate plane polynomial.

routes.title: Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers, Part II: class-group torsion and its applications
routes.brief: FIRST import Effective arithmetic bounds and geometry of numbers (tauceti:Completed/EffectiveBounds), including its completed discriminant, ideal-count and class-group APIs. Import Geometry of numbers, quadratic forms and homogeneous arithmetic (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic), GN.0/GN.1/GN.5, for existing lattices, covolumes and the planned genuine successive-minimum/reduced-basis theorems. Reconcile the pending EffectiveBoundsCompactModels proposal from PAPER-COUVEIGNES-20: share its measure and short-integer interfaces; do not create a second generic reduction theory or assume that unreviewed proposal is installed. Prove balanced generators for every class killed by m, the largest minimum bound, variable-radius box counts, ideal-square injection and the original degree-n signed norm-curve argument. Import Uniform integral-point bounds by determinant methods (IntegralPointDeterminantMethods) for coefficient-uniform Bombieri–Pila, preserving singular curves. For the reduced basis, use the trace-weighted metric, primitive vector 1, the GN.5 primitive-prefix construction and its product bound; then transport the largest-minimum conclusion to the ordinary Euclidean metric. The no-index-two norm-curve bound is D^(1/2−1/(2n)+epsilon). Import ordinary Hilbert class fields and conjugation/uniqueness from ClassFieldTheory Layer 13, not a new class-field carrier. For a quadratic E/F, construct the class-quotient coinvariants and prove r_2(E)≤2(r_2(F)+max(t,1)−1), counting finite and infinite ramification. Deduce h_2(E)≪D_E^eta h_2(F)^2 uniformly in F of fixed degree, then close the general-exponent theorem by strong induction on absolute degree using the quadratic D^eta base case. The original one-factor relative-genus-source-claim stays diagnostic and is not a premise. Import Elliptic curves, Part II: uniform integral-point estimates (EllipticCurvesPartIIIntegralPointBounds) only for HV and Brumer–Kramer inputs, which do not depend on the sharper torsion bound. Construct the smooth cubic norm family, separate rational generators, and solve the feedback inequality with a=1/[6(1−b/log 2)]. Export h₂(K)≪D_K^(a+epsilon) in degrees three and four; the latter needs G4 resolvent/tori closure including reducible algebras. Derive the integral-model Selmer, rank and integral-point exponents a,a,c=ab/log 2 in this consuming extension, avoiding a roadmap dependency cycle back into the HV supplier. Do not export the unverified hyperelliptic or del Pezzo claims. Suggested future files: TauCeti/NumberTheory/EffectiveBounds/ClassGroupTorsion/{Balanced,NormCurves,CubicFeedback,Resolvents,EllipticApplications}.lean. Definitions use existing carriers and the discriminating tests in the items. Independent-review correction: import the built TauCeti elementary-2 quotient/rank API, PolynomialGaloisGroups Layer 4 for the polynomial resolvent and ST.1 for its integral-order comparison. This whole route is rejected pending G3/G4; routing a diagnostic is not permission to assume it.

routes.title: Uniform integral-point bounds by determinant methods
routes.reason: Catalogue screen finds no coefficient-uniform algebraic-curve counting owner. RP.4 is finiteness, ED is certified algorithms, and LD.6 is Pila–Wilkie outside the algebraic part. Retain the inherited candidate, now with selected original proof interiors.
routes.brief: Prove original Bombieri–Pila Theorem 5: for an absolutely irreducible real plane curve of total degree d≥2 and N≥exp(d^6), the integer-point count in [0,N]^2 is at most N^(1/d)exp(12 sqrt(d log N loglog N)); deduce the coefficient-uniform epsilon form for all N≥1 and integer translates. The curve may be singular. Import Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations), SF.0/SF.5, for plane curves and proper intersection/Bézout, and Mathlib determinants, interpolation, derivatives and Taylor/mean-value machinery. Build monomial evaluation kernels, scaled derivative norms, Vandermonde determinant estimates, the integer determinant separation argument, auxiliary covers, leading-term avoidance, derivative-level partitions, the short-interval lemma, recurrence and bounded-slope arc decomposition. Keep generic linear algebra and algebraic geometry with their existing suppliers. Correct the lambda substitution and q≤p typo in the author preprint; resolve integer rounding of delta with the displayed constants (G7), including singular/boundary exceptional points. Tests include Y²=X³ (singular degree three), coefficient translations, polynomial branches with constant higher derivatives, the smallest allowed d,N, and repeated abscissae. Suggested file: TauCeti/NumberTheory/IntegralPointBounds/DeterminantMethod.lean. Sedunova’s printed uniformity is not a supplied positive-characteristic analogue; G9 must be resolved separately. Sixth-checkpoint refinement: use bp-integer-normalization, bp-contraction-iteration and bp-recurrence-constants, then delta=floor(2 sqrt(log N/(d loglog N))) with the derivative-monotonicity proof in bp-integer-optimization to obtain constant 11 without changing the threshold. For constant 12 use the explicit 8d^3 finite-integer-point graph cover rather than assuming the stronger O(d^2) whole-curve decomposition. Retain singular/critical fibers, horizontal boundaries, noninteger interval endpoints, inverse steep graphs and the strict N<1 stopping case. E1–E3 record the source-level corrections; G7 now retains exact generic supplier matching and independent verification. Earlier wording asking for an unwritten rounding proof is superseded by this refinement. Seventh checkpoint: import the five exact Mathlib supplier nodes (Taylor, interpolation, Vandermonde, finite polynomial roots and mean value). Their consumer adapters remain explicit; none supplies Bézout or global analytic branch continuation. Tenth checkpoint: use the promoted supported-coefficient, repeated-Rolle, entrywise interpolation-witness, Newton determinant, ordinary Taylor endpoint and absolute-remainder adapters. Rank/kernel is rectangular; the short-interval argument uses a lower derivative bound at its Taylor point, not the upper absolute-maximum bound. Keep full-column-rank row-minor selection, specialization nonzeroness/degree, monomial norm-product estimates, SF.5 Bézout and analytic branch/inverse matching explicit in G7. Eleventh checkpoint M1/D1–D3/S1–S3 supplies rectangular full-rank row-minor selection via a linear retraction and determinant multilinearity; normalized Leibniz product and monomial estimates with the constant-column factorial saving; and nonzero coordinate specialization, degree and fiber bounds. Import the exact generic Mathlib suppliers rather than creating rival matrix/calculus/polynomial theories. Proper Bézout stays SF.5; smooth branch continuation and inverse graphs remain explicit obligations. These steps do not certify the stronger whole-curve O(d²) cover.

routes.title: Elliptic curves, Part II: uniform integral-point estimates
routes.brief: FIRST import Elliptic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/EllipticCurves), especially Layers 4, 6 and 7 for local heights, the actual Mordell–Weil group, the existing canonical height and explicit descent, and the planned cohomological Selmer comparison. The pinned canonical height is h_x/2 up to bounded error, agreeing with Helfgott–Venkatesh; the roadmap prose uses twice that normalization, so write the conversion. Prove the HV height-sensitive S-integral bound with S containing infinity and all primes dividing the integral-model discriminant, all s and epsilon factors, and beta(t) exactly as extracted; then optimize using alpha and deduce #E(Z)≪epsilon |Delta|^epsilon exp((b+epsilon)rank). Decompose the original local repulsion, height-shell, positive-height lower-bound, sphere-packing, torsion and global height-upper-bound inputs before declaring closure (G3). The original Brumer–Kramer Proposition 7.1 still must be acquired to prove dim Sel₂≤dim Cl(A)[2]+2omega(|Delta|)+2 for the cubic etale algebra, including reducible A and maximal-order versus model discriminants. This extension supplies tools to EffectiveBoundsClassGroupTorsion and does not import its improved torsion theorem: final exponent-a Selmer and exponent-c point applications belong to that consumer, preventing a cycle. Keep spherical-code theory in its generic owner after audit, not a new duplicate here. Suggested file: TauCeti/NumberTheory/EllipticCurve/IntegralPointBounds.lean. Test rank zero, t=0 versus t=1, nonminimal models, bad primes and integral coordinate changes. The hyperelliptic and del Pezzo rows in the inherited item list are diagnostics with unresolved G5/G6, not proved exports of this brief. The independent review rejects this combined scope pending a corrected statement and owner split.

routes.title: Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations, Part II: quantitative Picard torsion bounds
routes.brief: FIRST import Global function fields, reciprocity and automorphic foundations (FunctionFieldArithmetic), FA.0/FA.1, which in turn consume the implemented divisor and Riemann–Roch theory of Algebraic curves (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/AlgebraicCurves). Do not reconstruct divisors, genus, section spaces, Riemann–Roch, finite Cl-zero or projective-space cardinality: the exact pinned declarations are listed. Import the existing AlgebraicCurves Layer-5 degree-one-divisor target and Jacobian challenge (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/JacobianChallenge) Layer D for the rational Picard/divisor obstruction; no rational point on C is assumed. Fix E of degree g, form the nonzero sections of L(2E) with even principal divisor and quotient by every nonzero constant. Construct the half-divisor class map and prove it surjective onto 2-torsion using Riemann–Roch and 2c=0, not an unjustified injection from a unique choice of effective representative. High-degree RR gives dimension g+1, hence #Pic⁰(C)(F_q)[2]≤(q^(g+1)−1)/(q−1) in every characteristic. Import general Jacobian torsion and p-rank from existing Layer E; in characteristic two only 2^f geometric points exist, f≤g. Treat gonality as base-field-relative data. The claimed stronger q^((1−1/n)g) bound is withheld at G9 until an exact function-field counting theorem, epsilon handling, uniformity in q and inseparable/characteristic-two branches are proved. Suggested file: TauCeti/FieldTheory/FunctionField/PicardTorsionBounds.lean. Tests: genus zero, curves without a chosen rational point, nonsquare constants, even divisors which are not global squares, and ordinary versus supersingular characteristic-two Jacobians. Sedunova with a q-dependent constant is an unproved candidate repair, not an imported theorem. E13 also requires a bad-reduction argument. The independent review rejects this combined route until the first-bound scope is separated from these unresolved targets.

85: /-- The **Minkowski Convex Body Theorem for compact domain**. If `s` is a convex compact symmetric
86: domain of `E` whose volume is large enough compared to the covolume of a lattice `L` of `E`, then it
87: contains a non-zero lattice point of `L`. Compared to
88: `exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure`, this version requires in addition
89: that `s` is compact and `L` is discrete but provides a weaker inequality rather than a strict
90: inequality. -/
91: theorem exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_le_measure [NormedAddCommGroup E]
92:     [NormedSpace ℝ E] [BorelSpace E] [FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [Nontrivial E] [IsAddHaarMeasure μ]
93:     {L : AddSubgroup E} [Countable L] [DiscreteTopology L] (fund : IsAddFundamentalDomain L F μ)
94:     (h_symm : ∀ x ∈ s, -x ∈ s) (h_conv : Convex ℝ s) (h_cpt : IsCompact s)
95:     (h : μ F * 2 ^ finrank ℝ E ≤ μ s) :
96:     ∃ x ≠ 0, ((x : L) : E) ∈ s := by
97:   have h_mes : μ s ≠ 0 := fun hμ ↦ fund.measure_ne_zero (NeZero.ne μ) <| by simpa [hμ] using h
98:   have h_nemp : s.Nonempty := nonempty_of_measure_ne_zero h_mes
99:   let u : ℕ → ℝ≥0 := (exists_seq_strictAnti_tendsto 0).choose
100:   let K : ConvexBody E := ⟨s, h_conv, h_cpt, h_nemp⟩
101:   let S : ℕ → ConvexBody E := fun n => (1 + u n) • K
102:   let Z : ℕ → Set E := fun n => (S n) ∩ (L \ {0})
103:   -- The convex bodies `S n` have volume strictly larger than `μ s` and thus we can apply
104:   -- `exists_ne_zero_mem_lattice_of_measure_mul_two_pow_lt_measure` to them and obtain that
105:   -- `S n` contains a nonzero point of `L`. Since the intersection of the `S n` is equal to `s`,
106:   -- it follows that `s` contains a nonzero point of `L`.
107:   have h_zero : 0 ∈ K := K.zero_mem_of_symmetric h_symm
108:   suffices Set.Nonempty (⋂ n, Z n) by
109:     simp_rw [Z, S, ConvexBody.coe_smul', NNReal.smul_def, ← Set.iInter_inter, NNReal.coe_add,
110:       NNReal.coe_one] at this
111:     rw [K.iInter_smul_eq_self h_zero] at this
112:     · obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := this
113:       exact ⟨⟨x, by simp_all⟩, by aesop⟩
114:     · exact (exists_seq_strictAnti_tendsto (0 : ℝ≥0)).choose_spec.2.2

67: on `(a, b)` and has the same limit `l` at `𝓝[>] a` and `𝓝[<] b`, then `f' c = 0`

70:     (hfb : Tendsto f (𝓝[<] b) (𝓝 l)) (hff' : ∀ x ∈ Ioo a b, HasDerivAt f (f' x) x) :

73:     (fun x hx ↦ (hff' x hx).continuousAt.continuousWithinAt) hfa hfb

77: `l` at `𝓝[>] a` and `𝓝[<] b`, then `deriv f c = 0` for some `c ∈ (a, b)`. This version
78: does not require differentiability of `f` because we define `deriv f c = 0` whenever `f` is not

  isCompact_Icc : ∀ {a b : α}, IsCompact (Icc a b)

65: /-- The Taylor polynomial with derivatives inside of a set `s`.

109: /-- **Every degree-zero divisor class contains a divisor of the form `A - n·B`, with `A` effective

111: (Stichtenoth, the representative step in the proof of Proposition 5.1.3). Riemann's theorem makes
112: `L(D + n·B)` nonzero, and a nonzero function in it moves `D + n·B` to an effective divisor of the
113: same degree. -/

115:     {B D : Divisor k F} {n : ℕ} (hn : (genus k F : ℤ) ≤ n * degree B) (hD : degree D = 0) :

58: /-- **Riemann--Roch in high degree** (Stichtenoth, Theorem 1.5.17): if
59: `deg D >= 2g - 1`, then
60: 
61: `ℓ(D) = deg D + 1 - g`.

63: The statement uses integers throughout, matching both divisor degree and the Riemann--Roch
64: identity and avoiding a truncated natural-number subtraction. -/
65: theorem dim_eq_degree_add_one_sub_genus_of_two_mul_genus_sub_one_le_degree
66:     (hF : IsFunctionField k F) (hex : IsIntegrallyClosedIn k F) {D : Divisor k F}
67:     (hD : 2 * (genus k F : ℤ) - 1 ≤ degree D) :
68:     (dim D : ℤ) = degree D + 1 - genus k F := by
69:   obtain ⟨W, hW⟩ := exists_isRiemannRochDivisor hF hex

72:     rw [degree_sub, hdegW]
73:     omega

75:   simpa [hzero] using Divisor.isRiemannRochDivisor_iff.mp hW D

/-- **The maximal elementary-2 quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` of the class group**, the general
`TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient` specialized to `ClassGroup R`. -/
abbrev ElementaryTwoQuotient : Type _ := TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient (ClassGroup R)

/-- The class of an ideal class in the maximal elementary-2 quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²`. -/
noncomputable def elementaryTwoQuotientMk (C : ClassGroup R) : ElementaryTwoQuotient R :=
  TauCeti.elementaryTwoQuotientMk C

/-- An ideal class has trivial class in `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` iff it is a square. -/
@[simp] theorem elementaryTwoQuotientMk_eq_zero_iff (C : ClassGroup R) :

/-- **The 2-rank of the class group**: the `ZMod 2` dimension of the maximal elementary-2
quotient `Cl(R)/Cl(R)²` (zero, by convention of `Module.finrank`, when the quotient is
infinite-dimensional). In genus-theory applications the `t - 1` formula belongs to the narrow
class group; for imaginary fields the narrow and ordinary class groups coincide. -/
noncomputable def twoRank : ℕ :=
  TauCeti.twoRank (ClassGroup R)

/-- The 2-rank of the class group is the `ZMod 2` dimension of its maximal elementary-2 quotient
`Cl(R) / Cl(R)²`. -/
@[simp] theorem twoRank_def :
    twoRank R = Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) :=
  TauCeti.twoRank_def (ClassGroup R)

twoRank R = Module.finrank (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) :=
  TauCeti.twoRank_def (ClassGroup R)

/-- The maximal elementary-2 quotient has cardinality `2 ^ twoRank`: it is a finite `𝔽₂`-vector
space of dimension the 2-rank. -/
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank
    [Module.Finite (ZMod 2) (ElementaryTwoQuotient R)] :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = 2 ^ twoRank R :=
  TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_two_pow_twoRank (ClassGroup R)

/-- Multiplicatively equivalent class groups have `Cl/Cl²` quotients with the same `ZMod 2`
finrank. -/

TauCeti.two_pow_twoRank_le_card (ClassGroup R)

/-- **The maximal elementary-2 quotient and the 2-torsion subgroup have the same cardinality.**
`|Cl(R)/Cl(R)²| = |Cl(R)[2]|`. -/
theorem card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion :
    Nat.card (ElementaryTwoQuotient R) = Nat.card {C : ClassGroup R // C ^ 2 = 1} :=
  TauCeti.card_elementaryTwoQuotient_eq_card_twoTorsion (ClassGroup R)

/-- A vector `v` in an integer module is primitive when some integer-valued linear functional
sends it to `1`. Equivalently, the cyclic submodule generated by `v` splits off a copy of `ℤ`. -/
def IsPrimitive (v : M) : Prop := ∃ f : M →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ, f v = 1

/-- A vector is primitive exactly when an integer-valued linear functional takes the value one
on it. This is the introduction and elimination interface for `IsPrimitive`. -/
theorem isPrimitive_def {v : M} : IsPrimitive v ↔ ∃ f : M →ₗ[ℤ] ℤ, f v = 1 := Iff.rfl

/-- A primitive vector is nonzero. -/
theorem IsPrimitive.ne_zero {v : M} (h : IsPrimitive v) : v ≠ 0 := by
  rintro rfl
  obtain ⟨f, hf⟩ := h

theorem IsPrimitive.exists_basis [Module.Free ℤ M] [Module.Finite ℤ M] {v : M}

sourceIssues.reason: Over odd F_q, take any irreducible f(T) and G=X^2-Y^2-f(T). Its generic affine conic is absolutely irreducible, but reduction modulo f is two distinct lines and has 2|f|-1 affine points.
